name: Cisco FTD
description: Cisco Firepower Threat Defense. FMC-managed firewall with a limited CLI, diagnostic LINA shell, Snort/IPS, and expert-mode Linux tools.
notes: FTD is managed by FMC; many troubleshooting tasks start in the FMC UI.
The diagnostic CLI is reached with 'system support diagnostic-cli' and exposes ASA-style commands.
Expert mode is a Linux shell. Treat it as root-level access and use read-only commands.

workflows.title: Packet capture from FMC
workflows.summary: Use FMC's packet capture workflow to capture traffic on an FTD data interface.

steps.instruction: In FMC, open Devices > Device Management, edit the FTD, then Troubleshooting > Packet Capture.
Select the ingress interface and add a match for the source, destination, protocol, and port.
Start the capture, reproduce the flow, stop it, and download the pcap.
Open the pcap in Wireshark and compare the pre-Snort and post-Snort paths if drop reasons are shown.

notes: FMC captures are bounded by the file size and stop control, so no persistent debug is left on the device.
If the capture shows traffic but the connection is dropped, inspect Intrusion Events and the connection event in FMC.

workflows.title: Open the diagnostic CLI and collect basics
workflows.summary: Enter the LINA diagnostic CLI, collect version, interfaces, routes, and connection counts, then exit.

steps.instruction: From the FTD CLI, enter the diagnostic shell. This prompt may ask for the enable password.
Exit the diagnostic CLI when finished. On some releases this returns to FTD; on others it closes the SSH session.

notes: Record the FTD version first; command availability changes between releases.

workflows.title: Packet-tracer — policy path
workflows.summary: Simulate a TCP flow through the diagnostic CLI's ASA-style packet-tracer.

steps.instruction: Read the result from the bottom up. Exit the diagnostic CLI when finished.

workflows.title: Connection and translation lookup
workflows.summary: Inspect connection counts, a source's connections, and NAT state in the diagnostic CLI.

workflows.title: VPN session inventory
workflows.summary: Inspect AnyConnect and site-to-site sessions, then confirm in FMC.

steps.instruction: In FMC, open Devices > VPN > Site-to-Site or Remote Access and compare the session state.

notes: If the diagnostic CLI rejects a VPN command, use the FMC VPN dashboards for that release.

workflows.title: Routing, interfaces, and ARP
workflows.summary: Collect interface, route, and ARP state from the diagnostic CLI.

workflows.title: AAA / RADIUS troubleshooting
workflows.summary: Check AAA objects in FMC and test a RADIUS authentication profile.

steps.instruction: In FMC, open Objects > AAA Server Groups and verify the RADIUS server, port, key, and timeout.
Open the identity policy or platform settings that use the AAA object and confirm the group is selected.
Use the FMC test button for the AAA object, then check the FTD connection event and the RADIUS server logs.
If the CLI is needed, enter the diagnostic CLI and check 'show aaa-server' with the group tag configured on the device.

notes: RADIUS shared secrets are write-only in the UI; confirm them by re-entering if authentication fails.

workflows.title: FTD health and manager registration
workflows.summary: Version, CPU, memory, and FMC registration state.
notes: If 'show disk' is not available in your release, use the expert-mode workflow.

workflows.title: FMC deployment and policy status
workflows.summary: Check pending deployments, task results, and the FTD's manager connection.

steps.instruction: In FMC, open Devices > Device Management and check the deployment status and pending changes.
Open Tasks to read the last deploy task and any policy or validation errors.
If the device shows as pending or unreachable, open the device's Advanced settings and inspect the FMC registration.

workflows.title: Expert mode — disk, memory, and logs
workflows.summary: Use read-only Linux commands in expert mode to check disk, memory, processes, and logs.

steps.instruction: From the FTD CLI, run 'expert' and enter the expert password.
Leave expert mode with 'exit'. Do not change services or files during an incident.

notes: Expert mode is a Linux root shell. Stick to read-only commands.

workflows.title: Snort / IPS event review
workflows.summary: Find intrusion events and determine whether Snort dropped the traffic.

steps.instruction: In FMC, open Analysis > Intrusions > Events and filter by the source, destination, and time window.
Open the event and check the action: allowed, dropped, or blocked.
Compare the event with the connection event in Analysis > Connections > Events using the same flow.
Review the access control policy rule and the intrusion policy that produced the event.

notes: If the connection is blocked before Snort, inspect the access control rule, NAT, and route.

workflows.summary: Inspect failover state and history on an HA pair.
